correctness.rationale: Every nonzero member diagonalizes through the invertible normal-basis Moore matrix to a Fermat-type smooth form, using p not dividing d. Field multiplication induces F_lambda(M_nu X)=F_{lambda nu^d}(X); the projective Singer group of order N has index gcd(d,N) power subgroup and exact uniform orbits. When the gcd is one, projective d-th powers permute all rational points; the nondegenerate trace pairing gives the full hyperplane-design incidence. For n=2,d=q+1 the gcd is one; the plane curve is smooth degree q+1 and has genus q(q-1)/2. In F3 the displayed polynomial identity with an invertible GL3 matrix is checked coefficientwise; exhaustive points F3, F9, F27 yield 4,10,28. Genus three, Newton identities and functional equation force L=1+27T^6. verify.py checks all critical arithmetic and the 13-block projective-plane design with VERIFY_OK; finite checks are not substituted for infinite structural proof.

originality.rationale: Asgarli--Ghioca--Reichstein (arXiv:2207.00918, Section 3) establishes the underlying normal-basis smooth system but does not state or imply the exact Singer projective isomorphism orbits, the rational point--hyperplane transport, the infinite degree-q+1 projective-plane design, or the thirteen-member F3 Klein embedding. Their diagonal smoothness argument alone does not determine the parameter action or the incidence on Fq-points. Meagher--Top (2010) and Dolgachev (2024) establish relevant classical Klein/Fermat geometry and twists, not the net incidence. Lercier et al. (arXiv:1403.0562) do not cover this F3 net. Related published projective designs and Klein zeta arithmetic are prior knowledge, not claimed new independently. Specific residual risk of unindexed older finite-geometry literature remains.

value.rationale: The maximal-dimensional finite-field smooth linear systems of Asgarli--Ghioca--Reichstein raise a natural arithmetic question about whether rational hypersurfaces vary in projective isomorphism class and how their rational points intersect. An exact gcd orbit law and a full projective incidence transport answer this across arbitrary q,n,d in the coprime range, producing a uniform infinite family of degree-q+1 smooth positive-genus plane nets with point design 2-(q²+q+1,q+1,1). The smallest plane quartic instance identifies the complete net with thirteen Klein quartics over F3 and determines all extension-field counts. The value is a structural/arithmetic connection of two natural constructions, not a routine isolated point count or a rebranded known curve.
